C0.quote: We study approval-based committee voting from a novel perspective.
C0.note: Randomized approval-based committee voting rules, with proportionality, stability, and differential privacy.

C1.quote: This polynomial-time algorithm satisfies EJR+ ex post, assures ex-ante monotonicity and neutrality
C1.note: Mostly design and analysis of randomized rules with stability bounds, lower bounds and a reduction. Also property satisfaction (AX). No strategic analysis.

C2.1.quote: A collection of all voters’ approval sets is denoted by 𝐴

C2.2.quote: An approval set of voter 𝑖 ∈ 𝑁 is a subset 𝐴𝑖 ⊆ 𝐶

C2.3.quote: each voter approves a subset of candidates, and a voting rule selects
C2.3.note: The intro says 'using voters' preferences', but voters are not given a held attitude separate from approvals in the model.

C2.4.quote: which we interpret to be the set of candidates that are “approved”
C2.4.note: Inputs are treated as approvals only; no held attitude is modelled.

C3.1.note: No analysis has voters misreporting. Strategyproofness is mentioned only in related work on DP.

C4.1.note: The paper uses no voter utility, welfare, satisfaction, cost or distortion notion in its results.

C4.2.note: The term 'dichotomous preferences' is not used.

C5.1.note: Ex-post proportionality (EJR+/JR) is the central evaluation criterion, framed as representation of voter groups.

C5.2.quote: a committee 𝑊 provides 𝛼-EJR+ if there is no candidate
C5.2.note: EJR+ is evaluated on the approval sets, with no statement relating them to held attitudes.

VOT.note: Voters supply approvals but do not act as agents in the model. In the dynamic model, an adversary changes one voter's approvals.

CAN.note: Candidates are only alternatives to be chosen.

ORG.note: The rule is the object analysed.

DES.note: The designer's choice is not modelled.

OTH.quote_behav: We assume that an adversary presents a sequence of elections
OTH.quote_info: We will assume an oblivious adversary.
OTH.note: Dynamic-model adversary presenting a sequence of elections. It is oblivious, with the sequence fixed at the outset, so NONSTRAT.

C8.1.note: No type is STRAT or MIXED, so this is NA.

claims.quote: suggesting their applicability in privacy-sensitive domains
candidates with similar sets of supporters should receive similar representation
which we argue is favorable from the candidate perspective

C9.1.note: Claims about institutions (blockchain, participatory budgeting) and fairness to candidates.

C9.2.note: Claims of fairness to candidates and of voter privacy need an assumption that approvals are sincere, to protect real preferences. This assumption is not stated. The claim of 'proportional representation of voters' also needs an input-attitude link that is unstated.

C10.1.note: No statement of a procedural reading.
